items.statement: The published evidence supports a small reduction in patients' post-traumatic stress symptoms with diaries read with a clinician, but does not show whether family-written entries add to that effect.
items.rationale: Need is high because the guideline depends on it; novelty is low because the review restates existing evidence for a local purpose; feasible within 40 hours.
items.risks: Overstating the single trial; missing unpublished programme evaluations.

items.statement: Reading support (timing, a trained clinician, screening beforehand) matters more for harms than who wrote the diary.
items.rationale: Harms data come from reading studies, not from comparisons of authors.
items.risks: Few studies report harms at all.

items.statement: Programme features (a named diary nurse, translated guides, an offer at the first family meeting) explain more of the variation in uptake than family characteristics.
items.rationale: The uptake study links a named nurse to higher uptake.
items.risks: Observational uptake data cannot separate programme and family effects.

summary: Three working propositions for the review; h1 organises the main section.
